newsitem.title: ITALY: Higher standard needed for local Bosnia polls - OSCE.
newsitem.headline: Higher standard needed for local Bosnia polls - OSCE.

text.p: The Organisation for Cooperation and Security in Europe (OSCE) said on Tuesday that extraordinary efforts should be made to ensure that local elections in Bosnia met higher standards than those of last month's national polls.

"We intend to hold the local polls on November 22-24 as scheduled, and with an extraordinary effort I believe we can achieve a higher standard than for the general elections," OSCE Secretary-General Giancarlo Aragona told Reuters after attending an international peace conference in Rome.

The OSCE, which has the task of supervising post-war elections in Bosnia as provide for in the Dayton treaty which ended the 43-month war, came under criticism from independent analysts for its handling of the September national elections.

Critics said the OSCE failed to take into account an extraordinarily high voter turnout and shied away from using its authority to punish violations of the Dayton peace accord, which required the vote be held under "free and fair" conditions.
Flavio Cotto, the Swiss Foreign Minister and OSCE chairman in office, said last week he believed political and technical problems could not be resolved in time for next month's voting.
But Aragona said the organisation was taking steps to eliminate the "difficulties and inadequacies" that plagued the national voting. He did not go into details.
"I believe that we can achieve a good result especially if we can count on the collaboration of all Bosnian parties," Aragona said.
Bosnian President Alija Izetbegovic last month beat a rival hardline Bosnian Serb to become the first head of Bosnia's new collective presidency in nationwide polls.
